title: Aller + infinitive
subtitle: Saying what you are going to do
explanation: Use je vais + an infinitive to say what you are going to do.

examples.eng: I'm going to make a reservation.
I'm going to hire a car.
I'm going to order a bottle of wine for the table.
examples.fre: Je vais commander une bouteille de vin pour la table.

title: Allez-vous + infinitive
subtitle: Asking “are you going to...?”
explanation: Use allez-vous + an infinitive to ask politely if someone is going to do something.

examples.eng: Are you going to make a reservation?
Are you going to hire a car?
Are you going to try the wine?

title: Ne... pas with aller
subtitle: Saying what you are not going to do
explanation: Put ne and pas around vais to say that you are not going to do something.

examples.fre: Je ne vais pas à Paris.

examples.eng: I'm not going to make a reservation.
examples.fre: Je ne vais pas faire une réservation.

examples.eng: I'm not going to eat here; the food is terrible.
examples.fre: Je ne vais pas manger ici; la nourriture est terrible.

title: Être: je suis / êtes-vous
subtitle: Saying “I am” and asking “are you?”
explanation: Use je suis to say “I am” and êtes-vous to ask “are you?” politely.

title: Adjective agreement
subtitle: Matching descriptions to masculine or feminine
explanation: Many French adjectives change form to match the person or thing they describe, such as occupé / occupée and fatigué / fatiguée.

title: Il est / elle est
subtitle: Saying “he is” and “she is”
explanation: Use il est for “he is” and elle est for “she is,” followed by a description or place.

title: Negating être
subtitle: Saying someone is not
explanation: Put ne... pas around the form of être to say that someone or something is not a certain way.

title: Est-il / est-elle
subtitle: Asking “is he?” or “is she?”
explanation: Use est-il or est-elle at the start of a question to ask about him or her.

title: S'appeler
subtitle: Saying what someone is called
explanation: Use je m'appelle to say your name or what you are called.

title: Avoir: j'ai / avez-vous
subtitle: Having something and asking if someone has it
explanation: Use j'ai for “I have” and avez-vous for the polite question “do you have?”

examples.eng: I have a ticket for Paris.

title: Direct object pronouns: le, la, l’
subtitle: Replacing “it” before a verb
explanation: Use le, la, or l' before a verb to replace a thing already mentioned instead of repeating the noun.

examples.eng: Do you want to try it?

title: Maintenant / plus tard
subtitle: Talking about now and later
explanation: Use maintenant for “now” and plus tard for “later” to make the timing of an action clear.

examples.eng: I'm going to the beach later.
examples.fre: Je vais à la plage plus tard.

title: Sous le nom de
subtitle: Giving the name on a reservation
explanation: Use sous le nom de to say that a booking or reservation is under a particular name.

examples.eng: I have a reservation in the name of Smith.
examples.fre: J'ai une réservation sous le nom de Smith.

examples.eng: It's in the name of Blanc.
examples.fre: C'est sous le nom de Blanc.

examples.eng: Do you have a reservation in the name of Descartes?
examples.fre: Avez-vous une réservation sous le nom de Descartes?

title: Vouloir + infinitive
subtitle: Asking what someone wants to do
explanation: Use voulez-vous + an infinitive to ask whether someone wants to do an action.

examples.eng: Do you want to try the cheese?
Do you want to make a reservation?
Do you want to do it now?

title: Question words
subtitle: Building questions with what, where, when, and why
explanation: Put a question word such as que, où, quand, or pourquoi before the rest of the question to ask for specific information.

examples.eng: What do you want to eat?
Where do you want to eat?
When do you want to eat?

title: Quel / quelle / quels
subtitle: Asking “which one?”
explanation: Quel changes to match the noun. This course introduces masculine singular, feminine singular, and masculine plural forms.

title: Combien / combien de
subtitle: Asking how much, how many, or how long
explanation: Use combien for “how much/how many,” and combien de before a noun. Combien de temps means “how long.”

examples.eng: How much wine do you want?
How many carrots do you want?

title: Pouvoir
subtitle: Saying or asking what someone can do
explanation: Use peux, pouvez-vous, or puis-je with an infinitive to talk about what someone can do or to ask permission.

examples.eng: I can bring some wine for Pierre tomorrow.
examples.fre: Je peux apporter du vin pour Pierre demain.

examples.eng: Can you call Marie at quarter past four?
examples.fre: Pouvez-vous appeler Marie à quatre heures et quart?

title: Devoir
subtitle: Saying what someone has to do
explanation: Use devoir to express “have to” or “must,” including je dois, devez-vous, and dois-je.

examples.eng: do you have to / must you
Whom do you have to see in Paris?

title: Negative question forms
subtitle: Asking what someone cannot or will not do
explanation: In these questions, ne... pas is placed around the verb to make a negative question.

examples.eng: Why can't I go with you?
examples.fre: Pourquoi ne puis-je pas aller avec vous?

examples.eng: Aren't you going to buy something for Marie?
examples.fre: N'allez-vous pas acheter quelque chose pour Marie?

title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Talking about completed past actions
explanation: Use j'ai + a past participle to say that you did or have done something.

examples.eng: I've ordered a bottle of wine.
examples.fre: J'ai commandé une bouteille de vin.

title: C'était / était
subtitle: Saying what something or someone was like
explanation: Use c'était for “it was” and était when describing what a person or thing was like in the past.

title: Past negation with n'était pas
subtitle: Saying something was not
explanation: Use n'était pas or ce n'était pas to say that someone or something was not a certain way in the past.

examples.eng: It was good but it wasn't perfect.
examples.fre: C'était bon mais ce n'était pas parfait.

examples.eng: Pierre wasn't there yesterday but he was there today.
examples.fre: Pierre n'était pas là hier mais il était là aujourd'hui.

title: Hier / aujourd'hui / demain
subtitle: Placing actions in time
explanation: Use hier for “yesterday,” aujourd'hui for “today,” and demain for “tomorrow.”

examples.eng: Pierre wasn't there yesterday but he was there today.
examples.fre: Pierre n'était pas là hier mais il était là aujourd'hui.

title: La même chose
subtitle: Saying “the same thing”
explanation: Use la même chose when you want the same item, choice, or action again.

examples.eng: I would like the same thing.
The same thing for me, please.
examples.fre: La même chose pour moi, s'il vous plaît.

title: La même chose que
subtitle: Saying “the same thing as...”
explanation: Add que after la même chose to compare your choice with another person or an earlier choice.

examples.eng: I would like the same thing as you.
examples.fre: Je voudrais la même chose que vous.

examples.eng: I have ordered the same thing as Marie.
examples.fre: J'ai commandé la même chose que Marie.

examples.eng: I'm going to do the same thing today as yesterday.
examples.fre: Je vais faire la même chose aujourd'hui qu'hier.

title: Encore vs un autre / une autre
subtitle: Choosing another of the same or a different one
explanation: Encore can mean another one of the same kind, while un autre or une autre can point to a different one.

examples.eng: I would like another bottle of wine (the same sort).
examples.fre: Je voudrais encore une bouteille de vin.

examples.eng: I would like another bottle of wine (a different sort).
examples.fre: Je voudrais une autre bouteille de vin.

examples.eng: Do you want another bottle? (a different sort)

title: Si c'est possible
subtitle: Adding “if possible” politely
explanation: Use si c'est possible to make a request softer by adding “if it's possible.”

examples.eng: I would like that, if it's possible.
examples.fre: Je voudrais cela, si c'est possible.

examples.eng: If it's possible, I would like it in green.
examples.fre: Si c'est possible, je le voudrais en vert.

examples.eng: I would like the same thing again, if it's possible.
examples.fre: Je voudrais encore la même chose, si c'est possible.

title: Ce / cet / cette / ces
subtitle: Saying this or these before a noun
explanation: French uses different forms of “this/these” depending on the noun: ce, cet, cette, and ces.

examples.eng: I would like this belt in dark grey.
examples.fre: Je voudrais cette ceinture en gris foncé.

examples.eng: I think this hotel is good but I prefer the rooms there.
examples.fre: Pour moi, cet hôtel est bon mais je préfère les chambres là.

title: Colours with en and adjective agreement
subtitle: Describing colour
explanation: Use en + a colour for “in [colour],” while colour adjectives can also follow a noun and agree when needed.

examples.eng: If it's possible, I would like it in green.
examples.fre: Si c'est possible, je le voudrais en vert.

examples.eng: Do you have that in white?
The light blue shirt is good but, for you, I prefer the dark blue shirt.
examples.fre: La chemise bleue claire est bonne mais, pour vous, je préfère la chemise bleue foncée.

title: Plus grand / plus petit
subtitle: Saying bigger or smaller
explanation: Use plus grand for “bigger” and plus petit for “smaller”; the adjective changes when it describes a feminine noun.

examples.eng: I would like a bigger car, please.
examples.fre: Je voudrais une plus grande voiture, s'il vous plaît.

title: Avoir mal à / au / aux
subtitle: Saying where something hurts
explanation: Use j'ai mal à... to say where you hurt. À changes to au or aux with some body-part nouns.

title: Je me suis cassé
subtitle: Saying you broke a body part
explanation: Use je me suis cassé + a body part to say that you have broken it.

examples.fre: Je me suis cassé le doigt.
Je me suis cassé le nez.
Je me suis cassé la jambe.

title: J'ai attrapé
subtitle: Saying you caught an illness
explanation: Use j'ai attrapé + an illness to say that you caught it.

title: Je me sens / je ne me sens pas
subtitle: Saying how you feel
explanation: Use je me sens + a description to say how you feel, and je ne me sens pas to make it negative.

examples.fre: Je ne me sens pas bien.
